saints.name: St. Frances Xavier Cabrini
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: The Italian foundress who crossed the ocean to serve immigrants and became the first United States citizen canonized…
biography: Born in 1850 near Lodi in Lombardy, Frances Cabrini founded the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in 1880. Longing to be a missionary, she was directed by Pope Leo XIII not to the East but to the West, to care for the poor Italian immigrants pouring into the Americas.

Arriving in New York in 1889, she and her sisters founded schools, hospitals, and orphanages across the United States and in Central and South America, some sixty-seven institutions in all. A naturalized American citizen, she died in Chicago in 1917. Canonized in 1946, she is the patroness of immigrants.
saints.knownFor: Founding schools and hospitals for immigrants in the Americas.
